Preservation Evoker Rotation in Midnight Prepatch

Preservation Evoker is an unconventional healer with a few unique mechanics that can make it a little more daunting to pick up, but it's also extremely fun once you do. Midnight removes quite a few buttons and interactions, which should greatly improve the accessibility of the spec. Here are some core concepts to keep in mind, especially if you're new to the spec:

 

 

 
 Use Short Cooldowns Regularly: Cast Temporal Anomaly the moment it comes off cooldown. It generates a lot of Echo buffs and heals for a decent amount via its absorb. Cast Dream Breath regularly when you do not have Echo buffs out.
 

 

 
 

 
 Cast Echo: Use your Essence resource and Essence Burst s and try to avoid wasting any of either. You will mostly cast Echo , but with the Twin Echoes talent, you might weave with Emerald Blossom .
 

 

 
 

 
 Consume Echoes: Consume Echo buffs with powerful spells like Merithra's Blessing (or Reversion ) and Verdant Embrace . More information on this choice in the rotation section. 
 

 

If you're looking for a more bite-sized rotation explanation, check out our simplified guide below:

Preservation Evoker Beginner Guide

 Best Preservation Evoker Healing Priority and Rotation

Both Preservation hero trees are extremely good so we'll look through the playstyle of each. In raid, both trees play very similarly with some minor differences in nuance and where your power is allocated. In Mythic+, the playstyles diverge a little more.

Hero Talent Master Switches

You can use the master switches below to flip the entire page's options to your selected choice. Bear in mind, current recommendation in all content is Chronowarden though Flameshaper is also a powerful tree.

Chronowarden
Flameshaper

 Chronowarden Raid

 Flameshaper Raid

Preservation has a unique Echo mechanic where two of your spells (Echo and Temporal Anomaly ) put Echo buffs on allies. The next spell you cast on any target will consume all Echo buffs you have out and duplicate whatever spell you cast to all of them. 
 
If you Echo target A, and then cast Verdant Embrace on target B then both A and B will get a Verdant Embrace heal and any associated effects.

If you put five Echo buffs out with Temporal Anomaly then press Reversion , then all five of them will get a Reversion heal-over-time effect. 
 


 

You'll get used to this quickly but I highly recommend logging in and casting a few Echoes around town to get used to how it works. This mechanic gives us superb flexibility in our healing style since we can prepare for damage by putting out Echo buffs and then consume them with a range of different spells depending on the situation we're in.

Tell me more about Echo

Echo also copies all extra talents you have for the spell that you consume them with. If you Reversion , then they will all:
 
Heal for 15% of the damage they took recently ( Golden Hour ).

Receive 10% more healing from you in the future ( Grace Period ).

Give you a 15% chance each of proccing Essence Burst .
 
We're going to cover which spell you should Echo later in this section, but you can see the potential. The only effect that does not Echo is Lifebind which is now limited to one target. Echo buffs also won't be consumed by Emerald Blossom - only Living Flame , Verdant Embrace , Reversion and Dream Breath - your core healing spells.

You'll often put out quite a few Echo buffs at a time before consuming them. This is sometimes referred to as a "Ramp" - a build-up of buffs before a big payoff phase where you heal a lot of people at once with one of your best spells.

Now that you know how Echo works, we can discuss what other abilities we'll be casting a lot and how the rotation all fits together. There are two key components to preservation healing:
 
 Echo and the spells you will consume them with.

Your short cooldown spells. Cast Temporal Anomaly as often as possible, and Dream Breath just after consuming your Echo buffs. They are expensive but do more than enough healing to justify it. As Flameshaper, we'll keep one Dream Breath charge on cooldown at all times and use both when we're in danger.

 Quick Chronowarden Priority List 
 
Cast Temporal Anomaly on cooldown.

Cast Dream Breath often. Cast it after you have consumed Echo buffs to avoid consuming them with Dream Breath .

Cast Verdant Embrace shortly after a Merithra's Blessing cast with 0-2 Echoes out. - 

Cast Emerald Blossom if you have an Essence Burst .

Cast Echo if you have Essence available and either no Essence Burst buff or you are at two stacks of Twin Echoes .

Consume Echo buffs with Merithra's Blessing (common) or Verdant Embrace (rare).

Cast Living Flame on the boss to farm Essence Burst s and contribute a little damage. You get a large mana refund if you cast it on an enemy instead of an ally.
 

 Quick Flameshaper Priority List 
 
Cast Temporal Anomaly on cooldown.

Keep one Dream Breath charge on cooldown. Cast the second when there is dangerous boss damage. 

Cast Emerald Blossom if you have an Essence Burst .

Cast Echo if you have Essence available and either no Essence Burst buff or you are following an Emerald Blossom cast.

Consume Echo buffs with Reversion (common) or Verdant Embrace (rare).

Cast Living Flame on the boss to farm Essence Burst s and contribute a little damage.
 

Explain Echo vs Emerald Blossom 

 VS 
The Twin Echoes talent incentivizes Emerald Blossom usage by giving us a double Echo on our next cast if we do. Emerald Blossom is also expensive, both in terms of mana and essence. However, Essence Burst removes both of those costs. If you have two bursts you can cast two Emerald Blossom in a row and then your next two Echo casts will each cleave to a nearby ally.

 Therefore, we should always cast Emerald Blossom when we have an Essence Burst . It's sometimes ok to cast an Emerald Blossom without one (mana permitting). It's acceptable to play without this talent if you'd prefer an easier playstyle.

Explain when to consume Echo with which spell 

 VS 
There are two primary choices: Merithra's Blessing and Verdant Embrace . Merithra's Blessing will be your primary choice but it is a proc so it won't always be available. Your core play pattern will revolve around farming Merithra's Blessing (each Echo and Emerald Blossom has a 20% chance to proc it) and then consuming your Echo buffs with it. If you get unlucky, it is ok to consume with Reversion in a pinch. Ideal play includes playing around your Dream Breath cooldown, since pressing Dream Breath guarantees you a Merithra's Blessing proc.

 Verdant Embrace 's niche is large healing absorbs since the amount it heals the primary Echo targets is higher than Merithra's Blessing (which heals for a lot via its cleave and flow-on effects instead).

 Remember that Merithra's Blessing also puts a full strength Reversion on the target with all associated effects! It is just a Reversion with a massive up-front multi-target heal attached. 

I'm having mana trouble 

Mana is a conundrum as Preservation because our most expensive spell ( Temporal Anomaly ) is also our most powerful. The best way to manage mana on Preservation, is to line up your casts better with the bosses damage pattern. It's very common to see players drop 50% of their mana in the opening minute of the fight during Bloodlust and to get very poor returns out of the spend. Even in Mythic raid, you can identify areas of the fight where you don't need to be casting Temporal Anomaly on cooldown. I would not recommend cutting any buttons (like Verdant Embrace) out of your rotation entirely. 

It's also possible to take the Energy Loop talent, which gives mana return on Disintegrate cast. If taken, you will use either Essence or Essence Burst on Disintegrate during downtime to recover. Whether to take Energy Loop or not is discussed more in the talents section of the guide, but you're only trading 2% healing or so to take it. Just this on a fight by fight basis but try and improve how you use your existing mana before you try to add more.

Further Explanation

 Chronowarden Mythic+

 Flameshaper Mythic+

Preservation has a unique Echo mechanic where two of your spells ( Echo and Temporal Anomaly ) put Echo buffs on allies. The next spell you cast on any party member will consume all Echo buffs you have out and duplicate whatever spell you cast to all of them. 
 
If you Echo target A, and then cast Verdant Embrace on target B then both A and B will get a Verdant Embrace heal and any associated effects. This is primarily how we will use Echo casts in Mythic+ .

If you put five Echo buffs out with Temporal Anomaly then press Reversion , then all five of them will get a Reversion heal-over-time effect. This is primarily how we will use Temporal Anomaly in Mythic+. 
 


 

Tell me more about Echo

Echo also copies all extra talents you have for the spell that you consume them with. If you Reversion , then they will all:
 
Heal for 15% of the damage they took recently ( Golden Hour ).

Receive 10% more healing from you in the future ( Grace Period ).

Give you a 15% chance each of proccing Essence Burst .
 
We're going to cover which spell you should Echo later in this section, but you can see the potential. The only effect that does not Echo is Lifebind which is now limited to one target. Echo buffs also won't be consumed by Emerald Blossom - only Living Flame , Verdant Embrace , Reversion and Dream Breath - your core healing spells.

You'll often put out quite a few Echo buffs at a time before consuming them. This is sometimes referred to as a "Ramp" - a build-up of buffs before a big payoff phase where you heal a lot of people at once with one of your best spells.

Mythic+ involves a mix of healing unavoidable damage, and mistakes your group might make. The former will get more difficult as you climb key levels, and the latter often gets easier as player skill improves. Preservation excels at damage you know is coming but has fewer responses to sharp damage on a single player. Let's look at what we have available to us:

Cast Combo on Cooldown - Reversion Uptime

 
 

 
 

This gives you a 100% uptime on the Reversion buff on the entire group and a very frequent shield on everyone.

Why is this important

 Reversion coverage puts a 10% healing buff on your entire group ( Grace Period ), covers small incidental damage they'll take via the HoT and in Midnight will also give them a damage reduction effect. Some of these do not scale with the power of the Echo buff you consume which makes Reversion a uniquely good spell to combine with Temporal Anomaly (which puts out weaker Echo buffs). These will also give you a chance to proc Lifespark - a good damage or healing effect.

Heavier Damage - Verdant Embrace 


 

 
 

 
 

When heavy damage is coming up you can use your Echo spell to put larger Echo buffs on your party. You can usually prioritize two DPS in your in your party plus yourself since the tank is not usually vulnerable to the same type of AoE damage as the rest of your party. Then, cast Verdant Embrace on whoever you didn't Echo . The Verdant Embrace cast is copied to your three Echo targets and all four of you will get a massive heal and a solid 8-second heal-over-time effect afterwards. 

Fitting in your other spells

Those will make up quite a lot of your healing but we have a few more useful spells too. Here are some common scenarios where they'll be useful:
 
 Dream Breath : Key Cast. Cast on cooldown at rank 1 if damage is low to moderate. Cast at rank 3 if you require a burst heal.

 Fire Breath : Key Cast. Massive AoE damage ability that'll also heal the party for a lot. Cast at rank 3.

 Time Dilation : Superb damage reduction for a single target. Low cooldown so use this regularly.

 Zephyr : Cast before AoE damage to reduce how much damage it does. You'll generally need to play through a dungeon a few times to pick out useful spots for it. 
 
We also bring quite a few powerful healing cooldowns that we'll discuss further down the page.

Spot Healing - Fixing Mistakes

Sometimes a single target will take a lot of damage at once. It could be the tank, or it could be from a missed interrupt. We'll respond to those types of events by casting Reversion on the target immediately, or if we think we have an extra GCD we can Echo -> Reversion . We're taking advantage of Golden Hour which heals back a portion of the damage they just took. We have two charges of Reversion so it won't interrupt your Temporal Anomaly -> Reversion plan from above. If they require more healing afterwards we'll use one of Verdant Embrace , Time Dilation or even a Living Flame if we're out of everything else.

Here's what you should do before every raid or dungeon:
 
Cast Blessing of the Bronze (our raid buff) - every pull.

(Raid) Make sure Source of Magic is active on another healer. Your highest HPS ally is a good target.

Make sure you have a Flask on - applied every 1-2 hours.

Make sure you have a Food buff - either every pull or every hour depending on the food.

Make sure you have a Thalassian Phoenix Oil on your weapon - applied every two hours.

(Optional) Apply a Void-Touched Augment Rune on - every pull. Can be expensive so lowest priority.

Cast Temporal Anomaly a few seconds before you pull. It'll give you some Echo buffs to start the fight with. 
 

You can read about the best Flask and food buff to use in the Preservation Consumables guide.

 Preservation Evoker Major Cooldowns

Preservation has access to some of the most powerful healing cooldowns in the game. Let's go through them and discuss where we might use them. Aim to pre-plan cooldowns as often as possible. Avoid scenarios where you're saving them "just in case", since this can cost you a lot of Mana through a fight and will increase the chance your raid suffers a death. Layer your raid's defensive cooldowns over the most dangerous moments of each fight to ensure you're covered.

 Stasis‎ 

 Stasis lets you store and then re-cast three spells, which means you can capture high value cooldowns like Dream Breath and Temporal Anomaly and cast them again in a big healing burst. Stasis can be quite intimidating to use as a beginner since it stores 3 spells for a subsequent, later use of them. This rewards pre-emptive, planned use since it takes time to store all three spells and you'll need the spells off cooldown too.

 How to play with Stasis 

How it works
 
 Stasis spells have no cost, no cooldown, and spells will trigger in the order they were stored.

For targeted spells, Stasis will send the duplicated spell at the same target . For spells without a target such as Dream Breath , Stasis will send the duplicated spell in whichever direction you are currently facing. 

Empowered spells will cast at whatever Rank the original was cast at.

Doesn't work on major cooldowns like Dream Flight , Rewind , and so on. It also only counts helpful spells, and thus can't be used as a DPS cooldown.
 
You have quite a bit of flexibility over which specific spells you Stasis , but you'll want to aim for high value ones where possible. 

Stasis Combos
Chronowarden Default Raid Combo
Chronowarden has some flexibility in how it builds its raid Stasis combo. Here we cast Dream Breath before we press Stasis in order to guarantee a Merithra's Blessing proc which we'll store in Stasis . Raid Chronowarden will also combine Stasis with Tip the Scales so we will have significant Haste via Temporal Burst . You might have to wait a moment for the second Temporal Anomaly to come off cooldown but it'll be short and it's worth it.

 
 

 
 

Flameshaper Default Combo
Flameshaper gets two stacks of Dream Breath but holding a cast to restore two stacks isn't particularly worth it when we have great alternatives. In raid it can be worth storing these at a low rank to get a lot of HoTs out on the raid to later consume with Emerald Blossom or Verdant Embrace . In dungeon content, consider upranking the Dream Breath cast instead so that you get a nice burst heal both when you store and when you release Stasis .
 
 

 
 

Pre-pull Cheese
If there's a key damage event early in the fight it is possible to store three Temporal Anomaly in your Stasis before the pull and then release it right before the damage event. The shield will absorb a ton and you'll have Echo on the entire raid. It's also possible to do this mid-fight but it's a little impractical since you'll spend 16-20 seconds doing nothing while Temporal Anomaly cools down.

 
 

 
 

Mass Dispel
 Cauterizing Flame s removes almost all dispellable debuffs and Bleeds from a target, but doesn't go on cooldown if it doesn't remove anything. That means we can store three in our Stasis in advance and fully clear the entire group with it. This is niche, but worth having in your back pocket.

 
 

 
 

 Stasis will require a lot of practice to master, and don't expect to play it perfectly at first. Once you're in the habit of using it to prepare for and handle high incoming damage, you'll find it's something you can't live without.

 Dream Flight‎ 

 Dream Flight is a large area AoE heal that'll send you in your chosen direction for 10-50 yards, healing everyone beneath you. It's a high-impact spell on a fairly reasonable cooldown, so you'll want to fit in as many uses as you can. It also adds a lengthy HoT to each target. Aim for a stacked group. 

 Dream Flight also applies a large absorb to you while you're in the air (equal to your health bar) which means you should be quite safe. This is removed the instant you land.

 Rewind 

Arguably the strongest healing cooldown in the game and certainly among the top 3. Rewind applies a 5 second HoT based on 33% of damage taken in the 5 seconds prior to you hitting the button. It also has a minimum value attached to it, and is doubled in dungeon content. You'll want to line this up with the most dangerous moments of every fight. 

 Evoker Deep Dives

In this section we'll cover different aspects of the spec in a little more depth. These are all fairly optional, but can be useful in increasing your overall understanding of the class. If you're brand new to the spec, I'd advise revisiting this section after getting some practice.

Overcoming a 30 yard Range

Preservation is unique in being the only Healing spec in the game with a reduced 30 yard range. This means that we're able to heal 56% of the area a standard healing spec can, and 44% of the area a Restoration Druid can. The impact of this varies a lot on a fight-by-fight basis - on some fights you'll barely notice it, and in others it'll be a major hindrance. Some tips to play around this limitation include:
 
Stand centrally wherever a fight permits. 

Set your mobility buttons to good keybinds and use them often. Hover , Verdant Embrace , Rescue , and Zephyr are all powerful, and between all of them you should have an answer to most movement requirements. Use Hover as your go-to, since it has the fewest restrictions. 

Adjust and update your planned positioning in between pulls. It isn't always possible to be in a great place, but you can at least be in a good one.

If you're about to run out of range of a priority target, put a HoT like Dream Breath or Reversion on them, or an Echo that you can consume later from any range.
 

In Mythic+, you're likely to find it an occasional annoyance. You might want to consider telling any group members to stay a little closer than they might otherwise so that they are easier to hit with Dream Breath .

Comment by madmurdock 
My little story: As like many I did my first Uldaman run with this char and yeah, this heal is really special. You are forced into melee to be able to hit your aoe spells and as soon your group spreads its becomming a disaster. We didnt wipe, we didnt even lose a man (was close though), but the 4th boss really put me to test. Some didnt know it and got hit by the fire circle and almost died, because I couldnt counter their mistake immediatly. Then everybody spread to their own mob and all the aoe spells dont work at all. At the last boss a mage stood too far away and was out of the 30 meter heal range. If you get used to the reversed life grip it could be fun though flying through the grp. :D

Evoker is really a pleasure to play in a melee group, but if there are ranged DPSes like hunter and shadows, that are used to standing away from the mobs, it may become troubling. If the ranged classes adept to this style, it will be a fun class, but if your allies sabotage you, you may end up having a bit less fun. :)
